paper.title: Profit Maximization in Bilateral Trade against a Smooth Adversary

settings.name_in_paper: Profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade against a sigma-smooth adversary
unmapped: Actions are DSIC and IR bilateral-trade mechanisms (monotone allocation regions in [0,1]^2 with Myerson payments): a non-parametric action space
Oblivious adversary chooses up-front a sequence of independent sigma-smooth valuation distributions on [0,1]^2 (density at most 1/sigma w.r.t. Lebesgue)
Learner observes the valuation pair (v_s, v_b) after each round, hence can compute the profit of every mechanism
settings.definition_quote: an (oblivious) adversary generates up-front a sequence $\cS$ of independent $\sigma$-smooth random variables... the learner gains $\prof(M^t, v^t) = \prof_t(M^t) \in [-1,1]$

settings.name_in_paper: Profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade against a sigma-smooth adversary (lower bound)
unmapped: Actions are DSIC and IR bilateral-trade mechanisms (monotone allocation regions with Myerson payments)
Oblivious adversary chooses independent sigma-smooth valuation distributions on [0,1]^2
Learner observes valuations each round (full information)
Lower bound allows the learner to know the smoothness parameter sigma
settings.definition_quote: Consider the problem of profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade against a $\sigma$-smooth adversary, for $\sigma \in (0, \nicefrac{1}{48})$.

settings.name_in_paper: Revenue maximization in repeated joint ads against a sigma-smooth adversary
unmapped: Actions are DSIC and IR joint-ads mechanisms (north-east monotone allocation regions with Myerson payments) for two buyers of a non-excludable good
Revenue is the sum of two payments each in [0,1], so lies in [0,2]
Oblivious adversary chooses independent sigma-smooth valuation distributions on [0,1]^2; valuations observed each round
settings.definition_quote: two buyers cooperate in an auction for a non-excludable good... The agents are characterized by private valuations $(v^t_1, v^t_2)$, drawn from a $\sigma$-smooth distribution... the revenue is: $\rev_t(M^t) = p^t_1(v_1,v_2) + p^t_2(v_1,v_2)$.

algorithms.name: Hierarchical Hedge (\hier; algorithmic chaining over grid mechanisms)
Joint-ads algorithm obtained by reduction from \hier

symbols.sigma_smooth: smoothness parameter of the adversary's valuation distributions (density at most 1/sigma), sigma in (0,1]

conditions: valuation distributions are independent and sigma-smooth, chosen by an oblivious adversary

source.label: thm:hierHedge
source.quote: Consider the problem of profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade against a $\sigma$-smooth adversary. We have the following regret bound: \( R_T(\hier) \le \frac{20}\sigma\sqrt{T}\log T. \)

results.notes: Regret is sup over mechanisms of sum of expected profit differences (sup outside expectation), hence pseudo-regret. Running time exp(sqrt(T)) as stated in intro. Algorithm does not use sigma.

source.label: cor:lower_bilateral
source.quote: Consider the problem of profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade against a $\sigma$-smooth adversary, for $\sigma \in (0, \nicefrac{1}{48})$. Then, for any learning algorithm $\cA$, the following lower bound holds: \( R_T(\cA) \geq \frac{3}{128}\sqrt{T}. \)

results.notes: Derived via reduction (Theorem thm:reduction) from the joint-ads lower bound of Aggarwal et al. 2024 (Theorem 8).

symbols.sigma_smooth: smoothness parameter of the joint-ads valuation distributions

conditions: valuation distributions are independent and sigma-smooth, chosen by an oblivious adversary

source.label: cor:upper_joint
source.quote: Consider the problem of revenue maximization in repeated joint ads against a $\sigma$-smooth adversary. There exists a learning algorithm which suffers regret at most $\frac{160}{\sigma}\sqrt{T}\log T$.

results.notes: Obtained by applying the reduction (Theorem thm:reduction, sigma = sigma'/4, regret factor 2) to Theorem thm:hierHedge. Revenue in [0,2]; mapped to bounded_01 with scale noted in unmapped.
